measured_by: CI=true npm run test:ci (the instrument CI uses), full suite, 0 failures, summary read within the same second as the run per this file's own stale-artifact warning. RAISED by Payroll 2's wizard work. `tests` is numTotalTests - it counts the skipped and todo that the 'passed' line does not (5547 passed + 5 skipped + 1 todo = 5553).
_what_this_is: A FLOOR, not an equality. A run that executes fewer files or tests than this has not tested what this number says it tests. Growth passes and prints a reminder to raise these. Removing tests on purpose means lowering these IN THE SAME DIFF -- the number may only move in a reviewed commit, never by drift.
_why_it_exists: 2026-10-07, run cap6_10 of a worker-cap experiment: vitest printed 'Test Files 338 passed (338)' while six files never ran, because [vitest-pool-runner] timed out starting their workers. The denominator fell from 344 and the summary line still read complete. vitest cannot catch this alone -- the six were never counted, so its own collected total was already 338. Only a number written down earlier can disagree.
_files_is: len(summary.testResults) -- NOT numTotalTestSuites, which counts describe blocks (a 2-file subset reported 4).
_the_arithmetic_of_this_change: +1 file, +17 tests, AND IT PAYS A DEBT OF MY OWN FROM THE PREVIOUS COMMIT. Counted per-file from a fresh summary, not inferred from a delta, because two offsetting errors also add up. EmployeeCreationWizard.test.tsx is the new file: 12 tests in c1ff17d8 (filterWizardRoles x8, buildWizardSubmission x4) plus 5 here (wizardOutcome). 385 -> 386 files; 5536 -> 5553 tests. 12 of those 17 should have been raised in c1ff17d8 and were not, so main has been carrying a floor 1 file and 12 tests behind since that commit - exactly the drift this file's _the_lesson describes, committed by someone who had not read it. The capture session found it, not CI, because growth only prints a reminder.
_the_lesson: A FLOOR THAT ONLY MOVES DOWNWARD IN REVIEWED COMMITS STILL DRIFTS UPWARD BY NEGLECT, and the drift hides the size of a later removal. Raise this in the commit that adds tests, not 'when convenient': had the floor been 5417, CI would have reported the deletion as -36 and the number would have matched the file.
_raised_in_the_same_commit: ⚠️ RAISED IN THE COMMIT THAT ADDED THE TESTS, which is the lesson the entry below records rather than a new policy. Earlier the same day the floor was 5 behind because growth only prints a reminder, and that drift made a later deletion report -31 when the file carried -36. The reminder is not a to-do; it is this edit.
_the_stale_artifact_finding: ⚠️ THE RATCHET READ A DAY-OLD FILE AND REPORTED GREEN. `test:assert-size` takes `.vitest-summary.json` as an argument and never checks that it describes the run you just did. Measured 2026-11-03: `npx vitest run` reported 384 files / 5494 tests, then `npm run test:assert-size` read a summary stamped Nov 2 14:06 and printed 'ran 379 files / 5385 tests; baseline 379 / 5385' — a perfect match, against yesterday. Only `test:ci` writes the file, and nothing couples the two scripts. In CI they run in sequence so the artifact is always fresh; run by hand, in either order, the ratchet can confirm a run that never happened. That is the same shape this file exists to catch, one layer out: a number written down earlier is worthless if the instrument reads a different run's output. ALWAYS run `CI=true npm run test:ci` immediately before `test:assert-size`, and check the file's mtime if there is any doubt. Reported rather than fixed — making the script refuse a stale summary needs a run id both halves agree on, which is its own change.
_found_by_a_peer_not_by_the_gate: ⚠️ CI PASSED ON THE STALE FLOOR, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN RATHER THAN A BUG: a floor passes on growth and prints a reminder. So the guard degrades silently and the only thing that catches it is a person reading. Had this stayed 12 behind, a later deletion of 30 tests would have reported -18 and read as a smaller removal than it was. Two sessions are editing this file today; whoever lands second must RE-MEASURE rather than add their own delta to the other's number, or the floor ends up below the truth by exactly the amount the first session added.
